This triggers a letter from Elminster, who retracts his previous support for Mystra's instruction, and tells Gale he has the option to find another way to defeat the absolute.

Elminster standing on a balcony attached to Sharess caress in Wyrm's crossing, looking outward. He's here to decry Gale on Mystra's behalf - Gale had a chance to sacrifice himself and destroy the Absolute previously, but hesitated. Now Elminster is here to relay the consequencs to him.

Elminster greets Gale after he's completed Sorcerous Sundries and learned how to reforge the Crown of Karsus, either outside the shop, or in camp. Elminster tells Gale that Mystra requires him to come speak with her in teh Stormshore Tabernacle, where he will learn the truth about the orb.

In this scene, Gale is conjuring an image of Mystra over the palm of his hand, staring at the goddess he’s love with, but who abandoned him. When the player approaches, he dispels the image and he feels embarrassed to have been caught doing what he was doing. The conversation turns to his passion for magic however, and he invites the player to try to cast a spell with him together. The player can do so by passing through various stages of spell casting, and when successful, this can lead to a first player-initiated romantic moment with Gale.

context: Gale is a powerful Waterdeep wizard who recently encountered a source of dangerous shadow magic and, following a sign from Mystra, chose to dispel it rather than wield it. Elminster responded to that decision with a letter and later an in-person rebuke—retracting his previous support for Mystra’s instruction, chastising Gale for hesitating to sacrifice himself against the Absolute, and saying Gale can seek another way to stop the threat. That message has left Gale emotionally raw: he still conjures images of Mystra in private and feels conflicted about his dependence on her. Nightwarden Minthara is trying to comfort him in camp, arguing that he remains a great practitioner of magic even without Mystra and that being free of her influence might ultimately be better.
